evidence.excerpt: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of the engineering principles underpinning postharvest preservation of fresh horticultural products, with emphasis on modified atmosphere packaging and cold-chain management. The chapter opens with a review of the biochemical and microbiological deterioration mechanisms that govern shelf life in soft fruits, including ethylene-mediated ripening, oxidative browning, and fungal pathogen proliferation. It then develops the engineering framework for MAP system design, covering gas mass balance modelling, film permeability selection, and tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration dynamics. Cold-chain management is addressed through the lens of predictive microbiology, explaining how primary and secondary models can be linked to temperature monitoring data to generate real-time shelf-life estimates. A section on supply chain integration discusses how MAP and predictive modelling tools can be embedded in digital logistics systems. Case studies drawn from Serbian berry export operations illustrate the translation of laboratory models into operational practice, including a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking discussion of emerging active packaging technologies and AI-assisted cold-chain optimisation. It is intended for graduate students and food industry engineers seeking a practically oriented reference.
